newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee lower on origins, Colombia news.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee lower on origins, Colombia news.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures finished Wednesday midsession lower with the market coming under origin selling pressure, principally from Indonesia, and depressing news from Colombia.
Benchmark July gapped $80 up as expected but turned back to finish the morning trade $22 down at $2,138 per tonne. Other traded months were also $17 to $25 lower.

Colombian Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said the government was opening "unlimited" coffee registrations for July to August, a period in which the country was expected to export 2.5 million 60-kg bags of coffee.
"This news dampens the spirit," said a trader.

Registrations opening on Wenesday morning for the two-month period would be "without restrictions". This means that private exporters and the Colombian National Coffee Growers' Federation were authorised to export all the coffee they could obtain.
But Ocampo stressed that no more than 2.5 million bags would be available for shipment, saying that "it's not a lot of coffee".
New York's July arabica futures finished 10.25 cents up at 264.20 cents per pound on Tuesday in an upward correction to the market's recent massive sell-off.
Traders called the market to open eight cents down on Wednesday based on London's performance.
Despite the Colombian news, traders said the short-term bullish picture remained intact in view of the current Brazilian winter.
The private U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said no damanging cold was in sight for Brazil's coffee areas but the colder weather this weekend bears watching.
